Byomkesh.description: The protagonist and truth-seeker, renowned for his detective skills and keen intellect.

Ajit.description: Byomkesh's close friend and chronicler, often accompanying him on investigations.

Birenbabu.description: A retired police officer from Calcutta, now settled in his ancestral home, who invites Byomkesh and Ajit to his daughter's wedding.

Neelmani Majumdar.description: A respected, retired police officer with a deep connection to the town and a central figure in the case discussed.

Sureshwar Ghose.description: A wealthy man suspected of murdering his wife Hashi; later found murdered in the same manner.

Hashi.description: Sureshwar's wife whose mysterious death is the focus of the investigation.

Binodbabu.description: A jeweller in the town known as Binod Sarkar or Binodbabu, who had a past relationship with Hashi's mother.

Kalikinkar Das.description: Owner of an iron and steel shop called Kalikinkar's shop, a friend of Sureshwar and one of the four card players.

Debu Mondol.description: A coal and firewood businessman, childhood friend of Sureshwar, and one of the four card players.

Bilash Dutta.description: A building contractor, friend of Sureshwar, and one of the four card players.

Dinamani Haldar.description: Hashi's legal father, known for his criminal background and frequent imprisonments.

Amala.description: Hashi's mother who had a troubled past and is revealed to be central to the family mystery; she had a past relationship with Binodbabu.

Major Burman.description: The civil surgeon who conducts the post-mortem examinations in the case.

Calcutta.description: A major city in eastern India, now known as Kolkata, historically significant as a cultural and administrative center.

East Bengal.description: A region that became part of Bangladesh after the Partition of India in 1947.

Partition.description: Refers to the 1947 division of British India into India and Pakistan, resulting in mass migrations and upheaval.

Lohapatty.description: A market area in the town known for its iron and steel shops.

Pujas.description: Refers to Hindu religious festivals, especially Durga Puja, widely celebrated in Bengal.

Holi.description: A popular Hindu festival known as the festival of colors, celebrated across India.

Ramdayal.description: A worker in Binod Sarkar's shop who helps identify the origin of the ornaments.

shehnai.description: A traditional North Indian wind instrument, often played at weddings and festive occasions.

babu.description: A term of respect or endearment for a man, commonly used in Bengal and other parts of India.

bail.description: A legal term referring to the temporary release of an accused person awaiting trial, sometimes used in Indian English.

ghat.description: A series of steps leading down to a river or cremation ground, commonly used for religious or funerary purposes in India.

godown.description: A warehouse or storage place, commonly used in Indian English.

dhoti.description: A traditional Indian garment for men, consisting of a long piece of cloth wrapped around the waist and legs.

kurta.description: A loose, collarless shirt worn in South Asia, often paired with a dhoti or pajama.
